tasks.gr10-literary-genres-text-features-t1: Topic: Literary genres and text features for Grade 10 English HL. Cover the novel, drama and poetry as genres; the parts of a book (title page, contents page, blurb, index, glossary, headings, captions); plot, setting, conflict, climax, narrator and point of view; theme versus subject; mood versus tone; stage directions, dialogue, monologue, soliloquy and dramatic irony; line, stanza, speaker, rhyme, rhythm and imagery. Ask learners to identify the genre of a short original extract, choose the book part that answers a need, and tell theme from subject or mood from tone.
tasks.gr10-language-structures-conventions-t1: Topic: Register, word choice and sentence structure for Grade 10 English HL. Cover formal and informal register, colloquialism and slang, verbosity, denotation and connotation, synonyms with different feelings, main and subordinate clauses, phrases, simple, compound and complex sentences, comma splices, paragraphs with topic sentences and linking words, apostrophes, its and it's, colons, semicolons and homophones. Ask learners to choose the right register, the right word for a purpose, to correct sentence and punctuation errors and to identify clause types.
tasks.gr10-essay-writing-process-t1: Topic: Writing an essay for Grade 10 English HL. Cover the stages of process writing (plan, draft, revise, edit, proofread, present), the Grade 10 essay in Paper 3 (50 marks, 300 to 350 words, content and planning 60%, language, style and editing 30%, structure 10%), narrative essays (opening, convincing storyline, direct speech, unpredictable ending), descriptive essays (senses, specific words, figures of speech) and argumentative essays (stance, body paragraphs with proof, conclusion). Ask about structure, purpose and editing choices, never whether a whole essay is good.
tasks.gr10-letters-cv-agenda-minutes-t1: Topic: Transactional texts for Grade 10 English HL. Cover purpose, audience and register; the Paper 3 transactional texts (two texts, 25 marks each, 180 to 200 words); the friendly letter (one address, date, informal salutation, first name); the formal letter (formal register, Yours faithfully with Dear Sir or Madam, Yours sincerely with a named person, surname and initials); the CV and covering letter; the agenda (items by importance, time per item) and minutes (past tense, resolutions word for word, attendance); the obituary (formal register, euphemism). Ask about format, register and content choices.
tasks.gr10-comprehension-summary-t1: Topic: Comprehension and summary for Grade 10 English HL. Cover skimming, scanning, context clues, inference, literal and implicit meaning, fact and opinion, emotive language, denotation and connotation, paraphrase, summary writing (main points, own words, leave out examples and repetition), concord, and the structure of Paper 1 (comprehension 30 marks, summary 10 marks, language structures and conventions 30 marks). Use short original passages and ask learners to infer, to separate fact from opinion, to choose what belongs in a summary and to correct language errors.
